items.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: Don Menza said “playing swing was a misdemeanor and playing bebop was a felony.”

ctx.x: I think it’s actually ideal for a music of this kind.

Yeah you could actually get tossed out of the practice rooms in some of the conservatories — who said it, Don Menza said “playing swing was a misdemeanor and playing bebop was a felony.” Oh gosh. Well did you come to a point ever when, in your late teens or whatever and maybe with your parents where you had a career decision to make? Was there ever a thought of trying to make a living as a jazz musician? And when did your interest in medicine start?

Well I think — I know that my music preceded my medical interest because I really was playing around at age two or three. But it was only a few years later that I started practicing psychotherapy without a license on the playground.
